properties.natural_language: Serialized container bytes received from an external data source must be validated against the container schema before deserialization: the container must have at least one field, at most 256 fields, no trailing zeros in active_fields, and the active bit count must match the actual field count.

Before deserializing SSZ container bytes from an untrusted source, the raw byte stream must conform to valid SSZ encoding structure and the active_fields bitvector must not contain trailing zero bits.
A Merkle proof received from an untrusted light client or smart contract verifier must include a valid proof path, field value, and the active_fields bitvector hash for collision protection.
After serialization completes, the serialized byte stream must be deserializable back to an identical container with the same active_fields and field values (round-trip property).
After deserialization completes, all fields not marked as active in the active_fields bitvector must be set to their zero/default values.

After Merkleization completes, the final hash_tree_root must include the active_fields mix-in, ensuring that containers with different schemas produce distinct roots even if field values are identical.

After successful Merkle proof verification, the active_fields mix-in must have been verified to prevent hash collision between containers with absent fields defaulted to zero and containers with explicitly zero-valued fields.
A progressive container must never have zero fields (empty containers are prohibited by the specification).
The number of active fields in a progressive container must never exceed 256.
The active_fields bitvector must never have trailing zero bits; the highest-indexed bit must always be 1.
The count of set bits (1-bits) in active_fields must always equal the actual number of fields present in the container.
Generalized indices (gindices) for fields in a progressive container must remain stable across schema changes — adding new fields must not alter the gindex of existing fields.
The hash function used for Merkleization must be collision-resistant; finding two distinct inputs that produce the same hash output must be computationally infeasible.

A sync committee message received via P2P gossip must be validated: the sender must be a member of the current sync committee, the signature must be valid over the correct beacon block root, and the message timing must be within the acceptable SYNC_MESSAGE_DUE_BPS window.

An aggregated sync contribution received via P2P gossip must have consistent aggregation bits and signatures, all included individual messages must be valid, and submission timing must be within the CONTRIBUTION_DUE_BPS window.
After computing the sync message due time via get_sync_message_due_ms(epoch), the result must be a valid millisecond offset within the slot duration, derived from the SYNC_MESSAGE_DUE_BPS constant.
After computing the contribution due time, it must be strictly later than the sync message due time to ensure individual messages are collected before aggregation.
Node clocks must be reasonably synchronized; the slot-relative timing for sync committee messages and contributions assumes clock synchrony across participating nodes.
The Phase0 fork choice logic (LMD-GHOST, justified/finalized checkpoints) inherited by Altair must remain correct and unmodified; Altair only adds sync committee timing extensions.
A consolidation request submitted by a validator operator must contain exactly 20 bytes for the source address, 48 bytes for the source pubkey, and 48 bytes for the target pubkey.
The fee payment (msg.value) accompanying a consolidation request must be greater than or equal to the computed exponential fee: fake_exponential(MIN_FEE, excess, UPDATE_FRACTION).
A consolidation request must not be queued if the queue has already reached the 262,144 capacity limit; excess requests are discarded without fee refund.
A validator exit request must be validated against the validator registry, and the exit weight must be computed from the validator's effective balance before churn limiting is applied.
After a consolidation system call completes successfully, at most MAX_CONSOLIDATION_REQUESTS_PER_BLOCK (2) requests have been dequeued and processed.
After a system call to the consolidation predeploy, if no code exists at the predeploy address, the block must be declared invalid.
After a system call failure during consolidation processing, the entire block must be declared invalid — system call failures are not recoverable.
After computing a validator's effective balance, the result must be capped at MAX_EFFECTIVE_BALANCE_ELECTRA (2048 ETH) regardless of the actual balance.

After checking the withdrawal credential prefix, only validators with the COMPOUNDING_WITHDRAWAL_PREFIX (0x02) may have effective balances above 32 ETH; validators with other prefixes are capped at standard 32 ETH effective balance.
The cumulative exit weight processed in a single epoch must never exceed the per-epoch churn limit (initially 256 ETH); any excess must be deferred to subsequent epochs.
A validator's effective balance must always be within the range [0, MAX_EFFECTIVE_BALANCE_ELECTRA] and must be at least MIN_ACTIVATION_BALANCE (32 ETH) for active validators.
The consolidation fee must always be at least MIN_CONSOLIDATION_REQUEST_FEE (1 wei) and increases exponentially based on excess requests above the target per-block throughput.
The predeploy contract at 0x0000BBdDc7CE488642fb579F8B00f3a590007251 must always contain valid bytecode; a missing predeploy invalidates the entire block.
The system call gas budget (30M) is completely separate from user transaction gas and does not affect base fee calculations or block gas limits.
Deferred exits must be processed in FIFO order across subsequent epochs as churn budget allows; no deferred exit may be processed out of order.

A transaction received for validation must have its first byte examined to detect the transaction type: bytes in [0x00-0x7f] indicate typed transactions, bytes in [0xc0-0xfe] indicate legacy transactions.
Transaction data must be correctly deserialized from RLP encoding before type-specific validation begins; malformed RLP must not bypass validation checks.
For a blob transaction (Type 3), blob gas consumption must be within the protocol limit before proceeding with further validation.
A blob transaction's max_fee_per_blob_gas must be greater than or equal to the current blob base fee.
A blob versioned hash must have the correct version byte prefix (0x01), be exactly 32 bytes long, and have a valid KZG commitment correspondence.
A blob transaction must contain actual blob data; a transaction that claims blobs but has none must be rejected with NoBlobDataError.
After transaction type validation, if the type byte is not recognized (not in {0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x03}), a TransactionTypeError must be raised and the transaction rejected.
After fee validation, the transaction's max_fee_per_gas must be confirmed to be at least as large as the block base fee, and max_priority_fee_per_gas must not exceed max_fee_per_gas.
Blob transactions (Type 3) must never be used for contract creation; any attempt to create a contract via a Type 3 transaction must raise TransactionTypeContractCreationError.
Contract creation init code must never exceed MAX_INIT_CODE_SIZE; any transaction violating this limit must be rejected.
The block base fee used for transaction validation must be correctly computed from parent block parameters; an incorrect base fee would lead to incorrect transaction acceptance/rejection.
After computing a CREATE2 address, the result must equal keccak256(0xff ++ deployer_address ++ salt ++ keccak256(init_code))[12:], with 0xff as a raw single byte (not RLP-encoded).
After a successful CREATE2 deployment, the new contract must exist at the deterministic address with the bytecode returned by the init code execution, and the address must be pushed onto the stack.
After detecting an address collision (nonzero nonce or existing code at the target address), CREATE2 must fail and push zero onto the stack.
After gas deduction for CREATE2, the total gas consumed must include the base CREATE cost (32000) plus GSHA3WORD * ceil(len(init_code) / 32) plus memory expansion costs.
CREATE2 must never deploy a contract at an address that already has nonzero nonce or nonempty bytecode (EIP-684 collision check).
The keccak256 hash function is collision-resistant; it must be computationally infeasible to find two different (deployer, salt, init_code) tuples that produce the same deployment address.
The EIP-684 collision check must be performed atomically before any state modification for the new contract; no race conditions may allow deployment to a blocked address.
CREATE2 may proceed at an address with non-zero balance (from prior SELFDESTRUCT) if nonce is zero and code is empty; balance does not block deployment.
An EIP may only achieve 'Eligible for Inclusion' status after rough consensus at an AllCoreDevs call; no EIP may bypass the ACD governance process.

An eligible EIP must have documentation linking to ACD meeting notes recording the consensus decision, conceptual support from core developers, and willingness from client teams to accept implementation PRs.
The EIP lifecycle must follow the sequence: Draft → Discussion → Eligible → Implementation → Testing → Accepted → Deployed; no stage may be skipped.

A Type 1 (EIP-2930) transaction submitted for signing must be detected and automatically converted to Type 2 (EIP-1559) format by the wallet; conversion must preserve the access_list and chain_id fields unchanged.

After conversion from Type 1 to Type 2, the transaction type field must be 0x2, max_fee_per_gas and max_priority_fee_per_gas must be set based on the original gas_price, and the gas_price field must be removed.

After field mapping from Type 1 to Type 2, the access_list must be copied unchanged, gas_price must be removed, max_fee_per_gas and max_priority_fee_per_gas must be set, and the type field must be updated from 0x1 to 0x2.
The network must support EIP-1559 and Type 2 transactions (London fork or later) for the conversion to be valid; converted transactions would be rejected by pre-London nodes.
The conversion from Type 1 to Type 2 must not alter the transaction's intent: the converted transaction must provide equivalent or better gas economics compared to the original.

An RLPx auth packet received from a peer initiator must be decryptable via ECIES with the recipient's static private key, and must contain the required fields: signature, initiator-pubk, and initiator-nonce.
Auth packet padding must use 100-300 bytes of cryptographically secure random data to prevent traffic analysis attacks.
A Hello packet received from a remote peer must be parsed with forward-compatible tolerance: version mismatches are ignored, additional list elements are ignored, and trailing data is ignored.
A UDP discovery packet must not exceed 1280 bytes; packets exceeding this limit must be rejected before further processing.
After successful auth packet parsing, all required fields (signature, initiator-pubk, initiator-nonce) must have been extracted regardless of version mismatches or additional RLP elements.
After a complete RLPx handshake (auth + ack exchange), both parties must be able to derive identical session keys for encrypted communication.
Unknown discovery packet types must always be silently discarded without error propagation to the sender; no error response may reveal information about the node's capabilities.
Tolerant parsing of RLP packets must never cause crashes or buffer overflows regardless of malformed input; additional list elements and trailing data must be ignored safely.
Only the ECIES encryption with the recipient's static public key ensures authenticity; attackers without the private key must not be able to generate valid auth or ack packets.
A wallet_requestPermissions call from a dApp must correctly identify the invoker origin without spoofing; the invoker URI must be validated against web origin conventions.
The permission consent UI displayed to the user must be resistant to clickjacking and UI redressing attacks; the prompt must clearly display all requested capabilities and caveats.

A URL included in a permission request must pass SSRF validation: the scheme must be in the allowed whitelist (http, https) and the port must be in the allowed port whitelist to prevent access to local services.
After a user rejects a permission request, the wallet must return a JSON-RPC error with code 4001 per EIP-1193; no permission must be stored.
After a user approves a permission request, the permission object must be stored in the wallet's permission array with the correct invoker, parentCapability, and caveats.
After a wallet_getPermissions call, the returned array must be filtered to contain only permissions belonging to the calling invoker; no cross-invoker permission leakage may occur.
A restricted method call must be denied unless a valid permission record exists for the invoker with matching parentCapability and all caveats are satisfied.
The wallet's permission storage must be protected from tampering by malicious extensions or local software; permission records must only be created through explicit user consent flows.

A raw transaction submitted via RPC or P2P must have its first byte examined for type detection: [0x00-0x7f] indicates typed, [0xc0-0xfe] indicates legacy; bytes in [0x80-0xbf] are invalid and must be rejected.
A typed transaction's TransactionType value must correspond to a defined and activated transaction type on the current network at the current block height.
Transaction signing data MUST include the TransactionType byte as the first byte to ensure domain separation; signatures omitting the type byte must be rejected.
After successful type detection and validation, the transaction must be routed to the correct type-specific handler; misrouting a transaction to the wrong handler is a critical error.

After successful signature verification, the recovered signer must match the claimed sender; type byte inclusion in signed data ensures a signature for one transaction type cannot be reused for another.
After transaction execution, the receipt must be encoded in the same TransactionType || ReceiptPayload format matching the transaction's type.
The first byte 0xff is reserved and must never be accepted as a valid TransactionType; transactions starting with 0xff must be rejected.
All nodes on the network must support the same set of activated transaction types at any given block height; disagreement on valid types would cause consensus failures.
New transaction types may only be introduced through the EIP process with security review; unauthorized introduction of new types could create consensus vulnerabilities.
